newsitem.title: USA: Illinois senator wants to extend ethanol tax break.
newsitem.headline: Illinois senator wants to extend ethanol tax break.

text.p: Illinois Democratic Sen. Richard Durbin said on Wednesday he will introduce legislation next week to extend an excise tax break for ethanol beyond the year 2000.

The current 5.4 cent-a-gallon excise tax incentive for fuel with ethanol is set to expire in 2000. But it has been attacked by House Republicans, led by Ways and Means Committee chairman Bill Archer, who want to cut or eliminate it.
But Archer, a Texas Republican, on June 24 backed off a proposed cut in the ethanol provision to 5.1 cents in his tax bill, saying he would support keeping it until it expires.

The Senate on June 27 defeated a proposal to eliminate ethanol subsidies after 2000 but is considering whether to gradually reduce the subsidy beginning in 2001. Archer's tax bill, which has passed the House, ends the subsidy after 2000.
Pressure to keep the ethanol tax break has been led by U.S. corn farmers and environmentalists. Most U.S. ethanol is made from corn and Illinois is the number two producing state.
"When it comes to the ethanol tax credit, we should be talking about extending it, not ending it," Durbin said at a press briefing with farm leaders.
